Subject: MAP: Technical evaluation plan and success criteria (post-call)

Thanks again for the great discussion this morning, Jordan. Quick recap and next steps so we’re all aligned on the MAP milestone for the technical evaluation: 

Summary of agreed scope:
- Redwood to provide a technical evaluation plan (benchmarks, test harness, model shortlist, target success criteria).
- Acme to provide representative sample dataset (redacted) and expected 95th/99th latency SLOs for interactive inference.

Proposed MAP milestones (draft):
1) MAP v0 (this week) — Draft technical evaluation plan (owners: Marissa / Camila). Target: 2027-04-29
2) Dataset handoff — Acme provides sample 5k queries and description (owner: Jordan). Target: 2027-05-03
3) Benchmark run — Redwood runs model shortlist on Acme samples (owner: Camila). Target: 2027-05-10
4) Results review + decision — Joint review meeting (owners: Jonas / Jordan / Camila). Target close: 2027-05-14

Key success criteria (initial):
- Quality: >= 85% task-level accuracy on Acme test set (we’ll define exact eval metric after dataset review).
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 250ms for single-turn interactive flows (p50 ideally < 120ms).
- Cost: per-1000 tokens cost below the threshold you specified on the call (we’ll put numbers in the plan once we have traffic mix).

Model shortlist (initial suggestions):
- open-llama-13b-quant (fast, cost-effective)
- redwood-vicuna-7b (balanced quality/latency)
- redwood-uni-70b (quality benchmark; run as reference)

Attachments: I’ve attached a MAP v0 spreadsheet with milestones and the Redwood benchmark plan draft. Camila will follow up with a proposed test harness and the exact commands we’ll run. 

Next steps for Jordan: please confirm the dataset handoff timeline and share any additional non-functional requirements (max concurrency, burst expectations, region constraints).

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and captures the conversation. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Quality metric: when you say 85% task-level accuracy, can we define that as intent classification + extraction F1 combined? Our PO wants the measure to be defensible.
2) Latency SLO — 95th <= 250ms is ambitious but aligned with our product goals. We have 5 concurrent users in the worst-case interactive flow; peak load is around 20 qps across the service. Can you confirm you’ll run the benchmark with concurrency=5 and report 95/99 pct?
3) Model shortlist — can we prioritize models that support 8-bit quantization and show a realistic cost estimate?

We’ll aim to share the redacted sample dataset by 2027-05-02 (one day earlier than plan) — I’ll upload to the Drive link you shared.

Great — thanks Jordan. Below is a concrete technical evaluation plan I’ll run once we have the sample data and access details. I’ll attach the test harness and example commands.

Proposed benchmark plan (high level):
- Test harness: local runner + Redwood-managed job that runs 3 warm-up passes then 10 measured passes across the sample queries.
- Concurrency: run single-client concurrency=5 (to match your worst-case interactive flow) and an additional batch-run at concurrency=20 to simulate burst.
- Metrics captured: latency p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, mem footprint, and exact output logits for deterministic eval.
- Quality eval: compute task-specific metrics (intent accuracy + extraction F1). We’ll generate a CSV with per-query scores for traceability.
- Cost estimate: we’ll report model runtime minutes and compute an estimated $/1k tokens using Redwood’s cost model; will call out differences for 8-bit/4-bit quantized runs.

Model shortlist and run plan:
1) open-llama-13b-8bit (primary cost/latency candidate) — run single-GPU, measure p95 latency and mem.
2) redwood-vicuna-7b-8bit (balanced) — run single-GPU and multi-GPU if mem requires it.
3) redwood-uni-70b (fp16 baseline) — sample small batch runs as quality oracle only.

Acceptance thresholds (proposed draft):
- Quality: task-level score >= 0.85 (intent+extraction combined) OR within 3% of your current baseline if you have one.
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms at concurrency=5. Flag p99 if > 600ms.
- Cost: candidate model must reduce per-1000 token cost by >= 20% vs current baseline OR meet the dollar threshold you provide.

Deliverables:
- Redwood benchmark report (CSV + summary)
- Recorded run logs and the harness scripts (sample-loadscript.py)
- MAP v1 with updated milestones and owners

I’ll start by validating the harness against a small synthetic set and then swap in your sample data. If you can upload the dataset to the Drive link and give me an account with read access I’ll schedule the benchmark runs for next week.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
